title: `VAR_*` and `STDDEV_*` of doubles cancel catastrophically
verdict: the textbook formula: 0 for 1e9 + {4, 7, 13, 16}; NUMBER inputs exact (SF-4)
description: Of the doubles `1e9 + 4`, `1e9 + 7`, `1e9 + 13`, `1e9 + 16`, `VAR_SAMP` and `VAR_POP` are 0.0 and so is `STDDEV_SAMP`; the sample variance is 30, which `VAR_SAMP(x - 1e9)` gives. The same values near `1e6` give 30. Over LINEITEM, `VAR_SAMP(l_quantity::FLOAT)` is `208.117…`, plus 1e9 `250.098…`, plus 1e12 `0.0`. That is the one-pass `Σx² − (Σx)²/n`, grouped or not. See [SF-4](../../../upstream/bugs/SF-4.json).
Of `NUMBER` values the result is a `NUMBER(38,6)`, exact to its scale (30.000000); `STDDEV` of integers is a double. A sample of one value is NULL, its population variance 0.
reference: `stat_algo`: any algorithm within `StatProps`' bounds, which the textbook formula is not (the bound here is about 5·10⁻⁴). sverify's SQL refuses `VAR_*` and `STDDEV_*` of doubles on Snowflake (`SnowflakeDialect.float_var`, this PR).

provenance.checked_by: sverify_dev.probe_snowflake through the Snowflake CLI (Snowflake characterization session)

evidence.sql: SELECT var_samp(x), var_pop(x), stddev_samp(x), stddev_pop(x), variance(x), stddev(x), SYSTEM$TYPEOF(var_samp(x)) FROM (VALUES (1e9 + 4), (1e9 + 7), (1e9 + 13), (1e9 + 16)) AS s(x)

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_snowflake` runs each query through `snow sql` (Snowflake CLI 3.32.1) on an X-Small warehouse, Snowflake 10.40.102, with the session's `TIMEZONE` set to UTC and `USE_CACHED_RESULT` off; every other parameter is the account's default, recorded in the header of probes.json (`WEEK_START` 0, `WEEK_OF_YEAR_POLICY` 0, `DEFAULT_NULL_ORDERING` LAST, `TIMESTAMP_TYPE_MAPPING` TIMESTAMP_NTZ). The inputs are literal `VALUES`, except the `sample-*` probes, which read TPC-H's LINEITEM (6,001,215 rows) in SNOWFLAKE_SAMPLE_DATA.
